content.text: {"headline":"Approve R1: shift breaks into quieter hours, cancel general coaching and deflect some status calls to chat. This lifts the 12:45-16:15 service level to 74.9%, short of the 80% target, for ₹225.","why":"The spike in general calls comes from the 10:15 home-loan SMS (MKT-2026-825) sent to 700,000 people. Loan enquiries are running at 2.02x normal, and service level has already dropped to 41.3%. With no action, the disruption window is predicted at 71.6% (general 64.5%) with 5.8% abandons. R1 is the best plan that follows policy. It raises the window to 74.9% (general 68.2%, payments 83.7%), cuts abandons to 5.6% and lifts the rest of the day to 83.6%. No policy-compliant option reaches 80% in the window.","trade_offs":["P2 (81.9%) and P3 (81.3%) are the only plans that hit 80%. Both rely on an IVR outage message, which breaks policy CX-01 because there is no confirmed outage or incident; the campaign is planned demand, not a fault.","R2 costs ₹309 versus ₹225 and adds tail cover, but scores the same or slightly worse in the window (74.8%) and only adds 0.3 points to the rest of the day (83.9%).","P1 costs the same ₹225 but gets just 71.8%, raises abandons to 6.1% and drops payments to 79.6% by moving agents across. R1 keeps payments healthy at 83.7%.","R1 delays breaks on both queues, so agents will work longer stretches before resting."],"watch":"General is still predicted at only 68.2%, so keep an eye on loan_enquiry volume and abandons through the afternoon. If the campaign keeps driving calls or service level stays well under 80%, bring in the duty manager to consider paid options or ask marketing about the SMS follow-up."}
